elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: §21.1 as rendered: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of ... The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims." Pre-existing mutual language retained unchanged.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Rendered §21.1 reads "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000". The USD 1,000,000 floor and the "paid or payable" basis are present, but the lookback is anchored to the event giving rise to the claim, not to the claim itself; these are not treated as equivalent temporal anchors. The deterministic check "preferred cap lookback precedes the claim" returned false, consistent with this reading.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: §21.2 retained: "Except for Excluded Claims, neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill..." — bilateral ("neither Party").

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: §21.3: "'Excluded Claims' means a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations..."; §21.1 caps liability "Except for Excluded Claims".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: §21.3 lists "data-protection, or security obligations" within Excluded Claims, which sit outside the §21.1 cap.
§21.3: "its indemnification obligations" is an Excluded Claim and therefore outside the §21.1 cap.
§21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" are Excluded Claims.
§21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" are Excluded Claims.
§21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" are Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: §21.3: "infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property" is an Excluded Claim, bilaterally framed.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: §21.3 final sentence retained: "Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section." Note the narrowing effect of the defined term "Fees" (§1.5 = Implementation Fee only), which is a pre-existing limitation rather than a defect introduced by the redline.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: §21.1: "each Party's total aggregate liability ... The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims."

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: §21.1 as rendered: "the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim". The fallback specifies no temporal anchor, and the edit removes the illusory "first Order Form"/defined-"Fees" limitation.
§21.3 includes "its indemnification obligations" in Excluded Claims, which are carved out of the §21.1 cap.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: §21.3 includes "a Party's breach of confidentiality ... obligations" in Excluded Claims.

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback level only. Every fallback element is met in operative language: the cap is mutual, is measured by twelve months of fees, and confidentiality, indemnification, gross negligence and wilful misconduct are Excluded Claims outside the cap.

Preferred fails on one element: the lookback anchor. Rendered §21.1 says "during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim", not "in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" as the preferred element requires. To close preferred, change the operative words in §21.1(a) to "in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" (or obtain confirmation that the event-based anchor is acceptable); the deterministic lookback check failed on exactly this phrase.

Actionable drafting risk (not an element failure): §21.1 now uses lowercase "fees" while §1.5 defines "Fees" as the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee. Vendor may argue the lowercase usage imports the defined term and re-creates the illusory cap. Repair by either amending §1.5 to mean all amounts payable under this Agreement and all Order Forms, or adding in §21.1 "(for this purpose, all amounts payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms, notwithstanding the definition of 'Fees')".

Related narrowness carried over in §21.3: "Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees" uses the defined term, so on a literal reading only the Implementation Fee is excluded from damages. If the payment-obligation carve-out is to reach subscription and other charges, the same definitional fix is needed.

Minimality holds: the only operative change is the cap basis in §21.1 (removing the "first Order Form" restriction and adding the USD 1,000,000 floor), both of which are within the targeted preferred cap element. No unrelated words were deleted, no survival tails, procedures or extra damages categories were added, and §§21.2–21.3 are untouched.

Intent preserved: mutuality, the mutual indirect-damages exclusion, the direct-damages characterisation of restoration/notice/incident-response costs, the Excluded Claims list and the payment carve-out all survive without contradiction; no cross-reference is left dangling by the edit.

Finding status "deviation" was correctly taken on the original text: the pre-edit cap was limited to "Fees" (USD 12,000 Implementation Fee) under the first Order Form only, well below six months' fees and therefore walk-away territory.
